newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Up to 30 dead in clash on Tajik-Afghan border.
newsitem.headline: Up to 30 dead in clash on Tajik-Afghan border.

text.p: Up to 30 people were killed when Russian border troops in Tajikistan clashed on Tuesday with armed Tajik Islamist opposition guerrillas trying to cross into the ex-Soviet state from Afghanistan, the Russian military said.
"The fighters lost about 30 men," the press service of Russia's Federal Border Service in the Tajik capital Dushanbe told Reuters.

A press service official said Russian soldiers, in a joint operation with Afghan border troops, had used automatic weapons, artillery and air support in the clash. He said Russian troops had suffered no casualties.

The official said that the clash broke out when around 80 fighters, based in Afghanistan, had tried to cross the Pyandzh River, which marks Tajikistan's southern border with Afghanistan, at about 2 a.m. (2100 GMT Monday).

It was unclear whether the armed group is loyal to the United Tajik Opposition, which is due to sign a peace agreement with the country's secular government later this month to end a four-year civil war. A ceasefire agreed between the two sides last December appears to have held.

Minor clashes occur regularly along the remote, mountainous border. The dramatic push north made by the radical Islamic Taleban militia in neighbouring Afghanistan has raised tensions along the war-stricken country's frontiers with the fragile ex-Soviet states of Central Asia.
